reasoning:
**What is asked.** Nvidia's percent price return minus Apple's, from the close on Friday 20 November to the close on Friday 4 December 2026 (Yahoo Finance adjusted close), in percentage points.

**Starting point.** Both returns start from a close that has not happened yet, so today's prices tell me about volatility, not direction. I centre on zero: over nine trading days nobody reliably knows which of two liquid mega-caps will do better.

**Why the range is wide.** Nvidia closed at $156.14 on 16 November 2026 (stockanalysis.com), down about 35% from $239.24 on 6 October, with daily moves of -9.3%, -4.3%, -5.5% and -4.1% inside two weeks. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on 12 November; CFO Colette Kress is interim chief and the board is searching for a successor (Kiplinger, 17 November). Results on 17 November beat expectations (revenue $115.8bn against about $108.8bn expected, next-quarter guide $130bn) and the shares rose about 4% after hours. Apple has been the steadier of the two: $356.27 on 13 November, up about 7% since early October, and it has held up while AI shares sold off. That lower correlation makes this gap a little wider than Nvidia's gap to Microsoft.

In calmer times I estimate the two-week gap has a standard deviation of about 6 points. With Nvidia's daily swings roughly double their usual size and leadership headlines still coming, I use about 9. The window has nine sessions (Thanksgiving closed, a half day on 27 November) and includes the November jobs report, due on 4 December. The Fed meets after it.

**What would move it.** A named successor, a return of Huang or findings from the board's investigation could move Nvidia 10% in a day either way. A relief rally in AI shares would favour Nvidia. Another leg down in the AI trade, with money hiding in Apple, would favour Apple.

**Forecast.** Median 0.0 points; middle half -5.6 to +5.6; 5th to 95th percentile -14.5 to +14.5, with about 9% beyond the ends of the -15 to +15 range.
